thread:
Mira: quick question — we're re-evaluating where routing logic should live for internal model inference calls. gateway-level routing (by customer tier/latency) vs pushing smarter routing into the client SDK. thoughts?
Sam: +1 to starting with gateway routing. centralizes policy, easier to iterate quotas+rate limits.
Leo: is there a perf penalty? gateway adds a hop. for low-latency requests that matters.
Mira: good point. current p95 is ~45ms intra-region. adding a gateway might add 5–15ms.
Ash: also think about telemetry coupling. if gateway owns routing, we can emit route decisions and tie to quota/dedicated capacity usage. client-side hides signals unless we add new telemetry hooks.
Kai: console UX concern — if routing is client-side then console rollouts/canaries for routing weights become harder to visualize. we need a single source of truth to show "route -> model variant -> success/latency".
devex-bot: FYI: SDK maintainers flagged changing client-only heuristics as friction for mobile + browser bundles.
Sam: another ops angle: gateways allow fast fallback policies (e.g., region fallback or cheaper model when Dedicated pool exhausted) without coordinating client releases.
Leo: what about protobuf vs JSON at the gateway boundary? if we keep internal gRPC/proto everywhere, gateway can do transparent transcoding for browser clients. but that implies maintaining proto stability.
Mira: I'm nervous about proto-first for product teams that iterate quickly. proto breaks surface is painful. we could adopt proto for backend-backend and JSON for public SDKs, with gateway doing proto<->json translation.
Ash: translation introduces escape hatches and mismatch bugs. telemetry should validate round-trip fidelity on deploy. add a canary that compares proto output vs json-path in staging.
Kai: rollout UX: propose we add a "routing preview" panel in console showing live sampling of decisions (10s window) with breakdown by tenant and route. helps product + SREs.
Sam: agree. quotas: if gateway handles routing, quota enforcement is straightforward (one place to deduct tokens). client-side requires server-side verification anyway so duplication is messy.
Leo: performance mitigation idea: edge router that does lightweight decisioning (hash + tenant tier) and only calls control-plane for exceptions. so common-case is fast, complex fallbacks go to gateway.
Mira: nice hybrid. runtime path: client -> edge-router (fast decision) -> regional gateway (policy + capacity check) -> model. fallback path same but with different model variant.
de v ex-bot: (typo) devex-bot: SDK changes required: expose routing hints and a small metrics callback API so clients can surface routing info to telemetry.
Ash: we should also add a server-side schema lint that checks proto->json mappings and flags lossy fields. run in CI for all model onboarding.
Kai: question for rollout: how do we A/B test routing policies? suggest "route experiments" in console where X% traffic uses new policy, with auto-revert on error budget.
Sam: auto-revert is must. tie to error budget + latency regression (e.g., >5% p99 degradation) and to cost delta for internal billing.
Leo: implementation note: keep routing rules declarative in repo (yaml) and versioned. runtime reads policy id and timestamp to ensure determinism for canaries.
Mira: action items: 1) prototype hybrid edge-router + gateway control-plane (Leo + Sam). 2) telemetry contract for routing events (Ash). 3) console "routing preview" + experiment UI spec (Kai). 4) SDK metrics hook plan (devex-bot). I'll kick off RFC draft.
Ash: +1, will draft telemetry schema with examples (routing_decision, policy_id, reason, model_variant, quota_charge).
Leo: I'll prototype a tiny edge router that does tier hash + fallback flags.
Sam: I'll spin up a gateway PoC that exposes policy API + quota ledger.
Kai: I'll sketch console mocks for preview + experiments.
Mira: thanks all — keeping this lightweight but want to decide before next release cycle. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deployment note — current canary infra supports weighted traffic splits; will wire into experiment UI once backend exposed. link: https://internal.ops/canaries/6123456789
Mira: nice, leaving notes in the RFC repo. will ping when draft is ready for review.
